newsitem.title: USA: NY developer plans 1.4 mln sq foot Boston complex.
newsitem.headline: NY developer plans 1.4 mln sq foot Boston complex.

text.p: New York City-based Millennium Partners, which has run into expansion problems at home, unveiled plans Tuesday for a 1.4 million square foot complex on a piece of choice Boston real estate.

The privately financed $250 million project will be anchored by a 4,700 seat Sony multiplex and a state-of-the-art Reebok Sports Club, mirroring the real estate developer's Lincoln Square project on New York's Upper West Side, the developer said in a statement.
But a spokesman for the Boston Redevelopment Authority said the city has not been formally informed of the size of the project and the developers have not yet filed those plans.
"If there are any tax breaks or incentives, I'm not aware of them," BRA spokesman Guy Bourgault said.

Meanwhile, Boston Mayor Thomas Menino, who has been trying to revitalize the city's downtown area for years, heralded the news saying the project known as Millennium Place "will bring life and energy (to the downtown)...Millennium Partners has a great track record of revitalizing areas and turning them into thriving urban destinations."

But Millennium Partners plans for expansion in New York City have hit a snag. They agreed to pay more than $300 million to the Metropolitan Transportation Authority upon signing a contract for the New York Coliseum just a few blocks from their Lincoln Square development. But New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani is objecting to the deal which is for a 64-story angular glass tower and connecting complex.

The developers' agreement calls for them to pay the money lawsuits or no lawsuits - and lawsuits are expected. It was the height of an earlier proposed building on the site that borders Central Park the contributed to that deal falling through.

Millennium Partners secured $300 million in June from Goldman, Sach's & Co's Whitehall Fund, financier George Soreo and his Quantum Realty Fund Ltd and a group of German investors to finance a new real estate fund that will five or six porjects totalling about $1.25 billion in various U.S. cities, the developers said.

Millennium Partners, in conjunction with WDG Ventures, is in the process of building a four-story, $180 million retail complex operated by Sony in San Francisco. Coincidentally, it was one of 30 corporations who do business with that city or need city permits to donate $10,000 or more to help underwrite last month's U.S. Conference of Mayors.

Millennium Partners has also paid more than $200,000 for air rights over part of the Massachusetts Turnpike in an area bordering Boston's highly prized Back Bay neighborhood. The plan there calls also for a similarly huge entertainment complex, residential towers, retail shops and a hotel.
